definitions.explanation: Morally wrong or corrupt in a fundamental way. Describes intentions, beings, or forces that are deeply harmful and malevolent.

examples.japanese: {邪悪|じゃあく}な{心|こころ}を{持|も}つ。
{邪悪|じゃあく}な{計画|けいかく}を{阻止|そし}しなければならない。
examples.english: We must stop this wicked plan.

examples.japanese: その{男|おとこ}の{邪悪|じゃあく}な{笑|わら}みを{見|み}て、{背筋|せすじ}が{凍|こお}る{思|おも}いがした。
examples.english: Seeing the man's malicious smile sent a chill down my spine.

notes: Common collocations: {邪悪|じゃあく}な{力|ちから} (evil power/force), {邪悪|じゃあく}な{存在|そんざい} (evil being), {邪悪|じゃあく}な{意図|いと} (malicious intent). Frequently used in fantasy, religious, and literary contexts. Can also function as a noun: {邪悪|じゃあく}を{退治|たいじ}する (to vanquish evil). The character {邪|じゃ} means "wicked" and appears in {邪魔|じゃま} (hindrance, nuisance). Related: {悪|あく} (evil — more general), {極悪|ごくあく} (heinous — even stronger), {悪意|あくい} (malice — focuses on intent).
